title: Bengal's Top Bureaucrat Was Just Its Election Czar
excerpt: TMC cries foul as BJP names ex-Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal as West Bengal's new Chief Secretary
body:
West Bengal's BJP government handed its most powerful bureaucratic post to Manoj Kumar Agarwal on May 11 — the very IAS officer who ran the state's contentious 2026 assembly elections as Chief Electoral Officer. The Trinamool Congress erupted in fury, calling the move a brazen assault on institutional integrity.

**What happened:**
Agarwal, the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal, was appointed Chief Secretary by the newly formed BJP government led by Suvendu Adhikari, according to an official order. His appointment comes within 48 hours of the Election Commission's special roll observer Subrata Gupta being named as advisor to Suvendu Adhikari, recalibrating the Chief Minister's closest administrative circle with former poll body top brass.

**Why TMC is furious:**
TMC former Rajya Sabha MP Saket Gokhale alleged that the BJP and the Election Commission were 'now being open about stealing the election,' questioning whether 'the courts are blind or complicit' and calling the development 'beyond shame.' Senior TMC leader Sagarika Ghose said the appointment 'undermines the credibility of the electoral process,' describing it as 'outrageous and brazen' and questioning whether anyone could still believe the Bengal elections were 'free and fair.' At the heart of TMC's anger lies Agarwal's oversight of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, which resulted in the removal of over nine million voters from the rolls before the election.

**BJP's defence and what comes next:**
The BJP government rejected the allegations, stating the appointment is strictly based on seniority and administrative experience, maintaining that Agarwal is the most senior serving officer in the state. Former Election Commissioner SY Quraishi noted there is 'nothing procedurally wrong' with the posting if he is the senior-most officer, though he acknowledged it 'definitely is bad optics' given the scrutiny surrounding the Election Commission's role. Watch for whether the Supreme Court — where TMC has told the court the SIR may have altered Bengal results — acts on the controversy, and whether Agarwal receives a service extension beyond his July 2026 retirement.
nri_angle: For Indian-Americans following democracy and electoral accountability in India, this appointment strikes at the heart of whether institutional separation between election administration and political governance can hold in a polarised Bengal.
author: Diaspora Desk
